verdict.rationale: Stripe documents broad API coverage across the core payments surface. Refunds can be issued 'by using the Refunds API or the Dashboard', disputes can be managed fully via API, and the hosted MCP server's generic tools can call 'any Stripe API GET' and 'any Stripe API POST, PATCH, PUT and DELETE method' across customers, invoices, subscriptions, payment links, webhooks, Connect, Issuing, tax, and payouts. A published OpenAPI spec and an in-browser Workbench Shell further show the Dashboard sitting on the same API. However, the evidence never states UI/API parity, and some functions are described only as Dashboard actions: creating restricted API keys, managing and revoking MCP access and OAuth sessions, and no-code invoice and revenue-recovery configuration. missing for 10: an explicit parity commitment or coverage statement, evidence that admin/settings functions (key creation, MCP access governance, revenue-recovery settings) are API-accessible, and independent hands-on corroboration of parity.
